facts.claim: Decision fatigue is caused by persuasion knowledge activation and reduced cognitive offloading.
facts.quote: Results show that decision fatigue is driven primarily by persuasion knowledge activation and reduced cognitive offloading, whereas trust calibration does not significantly predict depletion.

facts.claim: Perceived decision responsibility increases fatigue by discouraging reliance on algorithmic guidance.
facts.quote: Perceived decision responsibility further increases fatigue by discouraging reliance on algorithmic guidance.

facts.claim: Consumer fatigue from making everyday decisions is linked to the formation of brand loyalty and purchasing behavior in stores.
facts.quote: The hypothesis regarding the influence of consumer fatigue from decision-making on the formation of brand loyalty was confirmed.

facts.claim: Algorithmic personalization can reduce decision efficiency when interpreted as strategically manipulative.
facts.quote: The findings demonstrate that algorithmic personalization can undermine decision efficiency when interpreted as strategically manipulative

facts.claim: Persistent push strategies on short-video platforms may impose cognitive costs on young consumers.
facts.quote: However, persistent push strategies may impose cognitive costs.

facts.claim: FOMO motivates consumer engrossment and transient buys but also results in bad outcomes like impulsive spending.

research.angle: Algorithmic personalization and persistent push strategies can undermine decision efficiency and increase fatigue when consumers perceive them as manipulative.
research.verdict: The evidence confirms that decision fatigue is a real phenomenon driven by cognitive costs, persuasion knowledge, and perceived responsibility in digital environments.
research.caveat: The research on decision fatigue is specifically tied to short-video platforms and retail environments rather than all types of unlimited digital options.
